lesson.title: El Abrigo, El Vestido & Los Colores
lesson.subtitle: Describing clothing with llevar ('to wear/carry') and post-nominal color agreement

hook.title: Why 'To Wear' Is 'To Carry' (Llevar) in Spanish
hook.content: In Lesson 2002 you met **llevar** ('to carry') in time expressions (*llevo dos años aquí*). In everyday life, **llevar** is also the standard Spanish verb for **'to wear [clothing]'** — because you literally carry your clothes on your body! **Llevo un abrigo negro** ('I am wearing a black coat'), **Ella lleva un vestido rojo** ('She is wearing a red dress')!

pattern.title: Color Agreement Review Across Clothing
pattern.content:
• Masculine **el abrigo** ('the coat/overcoat'): un abrigo negro, un abrigo azul, un abrigo nuevo.
• Masculine **el vestido** ('the dress' — cognate with English *vest* and *vestment*!): un vestido rojo, un vestido blanco, un vestido hermoso!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I wear / I am wearing (lit. I carry)

exercises.target_answer: el abrigo, el vestido, un abrigo negro, un vestido rojo, llevo
exercises.meaning: the coat / overcoat, the dress (vest / vestment), a black coat, a red dress, I wear / I am wearing (lit. I carry)
exercises.explanation: llevar means both 'to carry' and 'to wear'; colors follow the clothing noun.

exercises.prompt: Spanish 'el vestido' ('dress / garment') shares its Latin clothing root with which four-letter English word for a sleeveless garment worn under a suit jacket?
exercises.meaning: vest, vestment, and invest ('to clothe your money in something') all come from the root of vestido!
exercises.explanation: Latin vestīre ('to clothe') gave Spanish vestir / el vestido and English vest and vestment.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'I want to buy a new black coat'?
options: Quiero comprar un abrigo negro y nuevo
exercises.target_answer: Quiero comprar un abrigo negro y nuevo
exercises.meaning: I want to buy a new black coat
exercises.explanation: el abrigo is masculine, and descriptive adjectives follow the noun.

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'It is a very beautiful red dress'
exercises.target_answer: Es un vestido rojo muy hermoso
exercises.meaning: It is a very beautiful red dress
exercises.explanation: el vestido is a masculine noun (-o), so both rojo and hermoso stay masculine!

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.meaning: I want to buy this blue coat
cues: I want to buy: Quiero comprar
exercises.affirmation: All 123 lessons of El Puente authored and verified!

summary.outcome: Describe clothing (el abrigo, el vestido) with post-nominal colors and comprar / llevar.

use_example.german: Quiero comprar este abrigo negro y ese vestido rojo.
use_example.english: I want to buy this black coat and that red dress.

summary.takeaway: Notice that el vestido ('the dress') ends in -o and is grammatically masculine: un vestido rojo!

abrigo.shift_rule: From abrigar 'to shelter from the cold'
abrigo.context_translation: I am wearing a black coat.
abrigo.etymology_derivation: llevar ('to carry/wear') is used for wearing clothes.

vestido.etymology_derivation: Related to English vest and vestment.

rojo.etymology_derivation: Latin russeus ('reddish') → rojo. Cognate with English russet and ruby.

azul.etymology_derivation: Hispano-Arabic lāzaward ('lapis lazuli') → azul. English azure is the exact same word.

verde.etymology_derivation: Ends in -e, so masculine and feminine are identical.

hermoso.etymology_derivation: Latin formōsus ('finely formed') — initial f- became silent h-: hermoso!

comprar.etymology_derivation: Latin comparāre ('to get ready, purchase') — English compare.
